messages.subject: Plotting the detection function when using encounter rates instead of g0
messages.subject_clean: Plotting the detection function when using encounter rates instead of g0
messages.body_plain:
Hi
I have noticed what I think is strange behaviour on the part of the plot.secr function when plotting the detection function from a model that uses the encounter rate (so lambda0 rather than g0). A simple way to show this is to use the detectfnplot function and to switch from the half-normal to the hazard half-normal forms:

> detectfnplot("HN", list(0.5,2000), xval= seq(0,15000, length=100))

> detectfnplot("HHN", list(0.5,2000), xval= seq(0,15000, length=100))

The first plot looks as one would expect with an intercept of 0.5, but the second plot produces a curve with an intercept of around or just under 0.4. Any idea what is happening here, is it a bug?

A secondary query relates to referencing factor levels via their labels. I have an example with a two level factor trap covariate and would like to estimate and plot the detection functions (using lambda0) for the different levels. I have made sure that the variable is correctly identified as a factor and then have tried plotting the detection functions as follows:

plot(model.fit, xval = seq(0,15000, length=100), lwd=2, col="black",  newdata=data.frame(factorvariable=0))

At first I noticed that the intercept seemed wrong and I think this is the same issue as above (it is correct if using a detect fn with g0). But secondly I have also tried to reference the label of the level as follows:

plot(model.fit, xval = seq(0,15000, length=100), lwd=2, col="black",  newdata=data.frame(factorvariable="label of level"))

and when I do this I get the following error:

Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = contr.funs[1 + isOF[nn]]) :
  contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more

I don't understand seeing what is causing this error as the variable is a factor variable with two levels.

Thanks!

Greg

messages.body_plain:
Hi Greg,

Regarding the detection function plot, I think I noticed previously that detectfnplot() always shows detection probability on the y-axis, even when the inputs describe the parameters of an encounter rate function. It seems to convert the encounter rate into a probability silently.

For example:

detectfnplot("HHN", list(1,2000), xval= seq(0,15000, length=100))

gives a plot with an intercept at about 0.65, and

detectfnplot("HHN", list(10,2000), xval= seq(0,15000, length=100))

gives a plot with an intercept at close to 1.

All the best,
Eric

messages.subject: Re: Plotting the detection function when using encounter rates instead of g0
messages.subject_clean: Plotting the detection function when using encounter rates instead of g0
messages.body_plain:
Yes. Internally both 'HN' and 'HHN' can describe  either the probability of detection or the cumulative hazard (expected number), as required by the context. They're interchangeable.

In this case I get
fithhn <- secr.fit(captdata, detectfn = 'HHN')
predict(fithhn)
#         link   estimate SE.estimate        lcl        ucl
# D        log  5.4846077  0.64702851  4.3558674  6.9058396
# lambda0  log  0.3069862  0.03413278  0.2470399  0.3814789
# sigma    log 28.7643439  1.30054758 26.3261891 31.4283043

# overlay 3 plots
plot(fithhn)
lines (0:200, 1-exp(-0.30698 * exp(-(0:200)^2/2/28.76^2)), col = 'red')
detectfnplot('HHN', pars = c(0.30698, 28.76), col = 'green', add = TRUE)

The curves overlay perfectly.

The axis label 'Detection lambda' is a bug. I see a note in the code from 2011-02-06 "revisit this" but I didn't! The problem arises with Poisson counts, whose treatment has shifted (there was a tendency earlier to confuse g0 and lambda0; see also the new secr-polygondetectors.pdf). I'll make another note to myself...

Murray

messages.body_plain:

Thanks,

Cristiano

messages.subject: Re: detection probability of each individual
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cristiano
It would help if you spelled out a little more what you mean. Under the SECR model, probability of detection is a function of location. The function pdot in 'secr' gives the probability an individual located at particular coordinates x,y is detected at least once during sampling. Were you wanting something else? The average across an area depends entirely on the extent of the area, which is not really useful.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
Sorry to not have a better question,

I just expected that each individual could have different probability of detection, and I would like to estimate this.

I did extracted the location of the individuals using:

oce<-fxi.contour (fit.0, i = 1:4, sessnum = 1, border = 7000, nx = 128,
    levels = NULL, p = seq(0.1,0.9,0.1), plt = TRUE, add = TRUE, fitmode = FALSE, plotmode = TRUE,
    normal = TRUE)
t(sapply(oce, "[[", "mode"))

> t(sapply(fxiout.ocelot1, "[[", "mode"))
      x        y
 [1,] 366050.3 8910838
 [2,] 362603.4 8914704
 [3,] 361564.3 8916123
 [4,] 361557.9 8916114

and estimated the detection of probabilities

> pdot(c(366050.3, 8910838), traps,detectpar=list(g0=0.001681018, sigma=1434.234),noccasions=8)
[1] 0.9825371

> pdot(c(362603.4, 8914704), traps,detectpar=list(g0=0.001681018, sigma=1434.234),noccasions=8)
[1] 0.8621421

> pdot(c(361564.3, 8916123), traps,detectpar=list(g0=0.001681018, sigma=1434.234),noccasions=8)
[1] 0.6299537

> pdot(c(361557.9, 8916114), traps,detectpar=list(g0=0.001681018, sigma=1434.234),noccasions=8)
[1] 0.635082

I would like to know if it is correct.

Thanks.

Cristiano

messages.subject: Re: calculating SD for secr estimates
messages.body_plain:
It's the SE that you need. As an aside - this confusion is why some of us refer to it as the relative standard error (RSE) rather than CV (although CV is so entrenched that it crops up even in 'secr'!). You should try derived(fsecr5), which calculates it for you. And when comparing RSE be alert to the effect of details=list(distribution = "binomial") vs "poisson" default. And equivalently derived(..., distribution = "binomial")

Murray
